components.name: Map rendering
components.purpose: Turns a stored map into the readable file kept beside the code. Also builds the boxes and arrows the browser draws.

components.name: Feature facts
components.purpose: Works out what each feature owns: its people, its decisions, its records and the doors reaching it.

components.name: Diagram builder
components.purpose: Draws every diagram, timeline and flow of one map, ready for the browser page to show.

components.name: Map server
components.purpose: Serves every map on this machine at a local web address. Reads a project's own code from its version history.

components.name: File browser
components.purpose: Lists a project's folders and files, marking each one by how far the map covers it.

components.name: Remembered projects
components.purpose: Keeps the list of project folders a person has opened, so each map is one click away next time.

entry_points.trigger: Opening the server's home address lists every project folder opened before, each one openable or removable.
Opening a project's own address returns the browser page that draws that project's map.
Asking `/api/recents` re-reads the remembered folders and says which of their maps can be opened.
Asking `/api/browse` lists the folders inside one folder, marking each folder that holds a map.
Posting to `/api/open` remembers a folder and starts serving the map inside it.
Posting to `/api/forget` drops a folder from the remembered list and stops serving its map.
Posting to `/api/reorder` saves a new order for the remembered project folders.
Asking `/static` returns the shared script or stylesheet every map page is drawn with.
Asking `/api/view` returns every diagram, flow and colour the page needs for one map.
Asking `/api/rawmap` returns the stored map exactly as its file holds it, byte for byte.
Asking `/api/tree` returns the project's folders and files, each marked by how far the map covers it.
Asking `/api/symbols` returns every function and class name found in the project at the map's commit.
Asking `/api/src` returns one file's text, read at the map's commit or at another one named in the request.
Asking `/api/health` says the server is answering and names the commit this map is pinned to.
Asking `/api/impact` says what a code change between two commits does to the map.
Asking `/api/impactcommits` lists the commits before and after the one this map is pinned to.
Asking `/api/impactsrcdiff` returns one file's line-by-line changes between two commits.
Asking `/api/dev-reload` says whether the viewer's own files changed, so a map page can reload itself.
Starting the server reads the remembered folders and loads every map still found there.
A map page opened in developer mode asks the server every second whether the viewer's files changed.

observability.signal: Stale-code warning on the server's console
observability.where_emitted: Printed to the terminal running the map server, at most once every two seconds, when the tool's own code has changed since the server started.
observability.where_viewed: The terminal the person started the server in.
observability.alerts: Nothing is configured; nobody is notified.

observability.where_emitted: Nothing is emitted. The server's own per-request log line is deliberately switched off.

config.purpose: Stops a finished build from adding its project to the remembered list.
config.default: Not set, so every build registers its project.
config.per_env: Nothing is set per environment. The map-quality scoring run sets it so its throwaway maps never appear.
